components.css: .ds-chips { display: flex; gap: 8px; } .ds-chip { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; height: 32px; border: 1px dashed var(--faint); border-radius: 6px; background: var(--raised); color: var(--ink-2); font: 500 12px/20px system-ui, sans-serif; transition: background-color 150ms; } .ds-chip:hover { background: var(--hover); } .ds-chip button { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; height: 100%; padding: 0 10px; border: 0; background: none; color: inherit; font: inherit; cursor: pointer; } .ds-chip:not(.ds-chip-on) svg { color: var(--faint); } .ds-chip-on { border: 1px solid var(--accent-line); background: var(--accent-soft); color: var(--accent-ink); } .ds-chip-on:hover { background: var(--accent-soft); } .ds-chip-on button + button { padding: 0 8px 0 0; } .ds-chip button:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent); outline-offset: 1px; border-radius: 4px; }

narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Quiet Console"**

azure-lupa is the category standard for cloud inventory, built to modern Azure Portal (Fluent) craft and then made faster: one table, one details drawer, no blade stacking. The screen is white ground and slate ink, divided by 1px hairlines, with one blue reserved for what the engineer is acting on. Nothing decorates. Density is high (30px rows, 13px body) but every row stays legible, and every machine string (types, IDs, API versions, CLI commands) is set in monospace so it reads as data.

The shell is three fixed regions: a 272px slate-50 sidebar tree (tenants, subscriptions, resource groups with counts), a main column (56px tab bar with breadcrumb and cache age, toolbar of search and filter chips, sticky-header table, totals footer), and an optional 460px details drawer at the right. The dark theme mirrors the light one on slate-950 rather than reinterpreting it. Keyboard hints (`kbd`) are part of the visual vocabulary, not an afterthought.

The world refuses novelty theming: no brand illustration, no gradients, no display type, no colored side stripes. Depth comes from tone and hairlines; shadows exist only on things that float.
keyCharacteristics: White ground, slate-50 chrome (sidebar, table header, footers), slate ink.
One blue accent for selection, focus and actions; a lighter blue (#60a5fa) carries the same role on the dark ground.
System UI sans for all text; ui-monospace for machine strings; tabular numerals everywhere.
1px slate hairlines as the only structure; overlay shadows only on floating layers.
Dense, keyboard-first: 30px rows, 28 to 32px controls, visible `kbd` hints.

rules.name: The One Blue Rule
rules.body: Blue marks only what is selected, focused, or actionable. Headings, tabs, icons and borders at rest are slate. The active tab underline is ink, not blue.

rules.name: The Lighter Blue in the Dark Rule
rules.body: On the dark ground the accent is #60a5fa, not #2563eb, so actions and focus keep contrast; accent-ink lightens to #93c5fd and accent-soft deepens to navy (#172554). Never carry the light-theme blue into dark.

rules.name: The Mirror Rule
rules.body: Dark theme is the same token set re-valued on slate-950; components never branch on theme, they only read semantic tokens.

rules.name: The Machine-String Rule
rules.body: If Azure or the CLI produced the string (type, ID, API version, command, JSON), it is set in mono. Human names stay in sans.

rules.name: The Numbers Line Up Rule
rules.body: Tabular numerals are on globally; counts align in every column and tree.

rules.name: The Drop, Don't Clip Rule
rules.body: When space shrinks, the table sheds information instead of cutting it at an edge: with the details panel open the SKU and Tags columns drop; below 640px each row becomes a 52px stacked single column (name, then type and resource group); long resource-group names are middle-truncated by measurement so both ends stay readable, with the full name in the tooltip.

rules.name: The Only Floaters Cast Shadows Rule
rules.body: Cards, panels, rows and buttons at rest have no shadow. If it does not float over other content, it does not cast one.

dos: Do use accent only for selection, focus and actions, and switch to the lighter dark-theme blue (#60a5fa) on the dark ground.
Do show selection as accent-soft fill with accent-ink text.
Do set every machine string (types, IDs, API versions, CLI commands, JSON) in mono.
Do drop low-priority columns, stack rows below 640px, or middle-truncate long names before letting content clip at an edge.
Do separate regions with 1px hairlines and tone (paper, slate-50, raised) rather than shadows.
Do keep controls at 28px or 32px and rows at 30px; keep the 4px spacing grid.
Do show keyboard affordances with `kbd` keys (11px mono, hairline border, 4px radius).
Do use dashed faint borders only for things the user can add or must do (unapplied filters, sign-in needed).
donts: Don't mark selection with a colored side stripe or a thicker border.
Don't use blue for headings, tab underlines, resting icons or decoration.
Don't put drop shadows on resting surfaces (cards, panels, rows, buttons); only popovers, the mobile drawer and the toast cast the overlay shadow.
Don't put white text or glyphs on the accent fill in the dark theme; #60a5fa is too light for white.
Don't add a display typeface, gradients, illustration or themed decoration; the product is the category standard.
Don't introduce uppercase eyebrow or kicker labels above headings; the sidebar's tree section header is the only uppercase text.
Don't clip a column at the details-panel edge; drop it.
